subject.title: feat(tui): add /upload command for file context

question: Should the core TUI own and reserve a built-in `/upload` command that reads local files into the next chat turn, or should this route through existing Gateway/plugin/file-context attachment boundaries first?
rationale: The workflow is useful, but the permanent command namespace and local-file ingestion boundary affect dynamic plugin commands and prompt-injection guardrails, so automation should not choose that product/API direction.

options.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
options.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require a rebase plus dependency, alias, lifecycle, bounded-read, and untrusted-wrapper repairs before merge.

options.title: Use Existing Attachment Boundaries
options.body: Pause this branch and ask for a narrower implementation that sends files through the Gateway attachment or input-file path so existing safety and provenance rules apply.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Keep or close the branch until a maintainer sponsors local file-context UX across CLI, TUI, and Gateway consistently.

recommendation.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
recommendation.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require a rebase plus dependency, alias, lifecycle, bounded-read, and untrusted-wrapper repairs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main TUI command/session lifecycle work makes steipete the clearest owner for the command and safety-boundary choice.
